newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPANISH PLAYERS THREATEN STRIKE OVER CHRISTMAS BREAK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH PLAYERS THREATEN STRIKE OVER CHRISTMAS BREAK.

text.p: Spanish players who want their traditional Christmas break are threatening to go on strike on December 29th.

"In the past six months the clubs have been unable to agree on anything, except to form a common front against the players," said Gerardo Gonzalez, president of the Association of Spanish Footballers.
Gonzalez has proposed to move the league programme scheduled for December 29th to January 22nd, creating a two-week break lasting from December 22nd to January 5th.
In recent years the Spanish league -- which starts at the beginning of September and finishes at the end of June -- has closed down completely from before Christmas until after New Year.

But a calendar already bloated by an expanded European club calendar and World Cup qualifying games has been stretched further to accomodate the 22-team first division that arose from a legal bungle in the summer of 1995.
Automatic relegation of four sides will mean that the first division will be scaled back to 20 teams at the end of this season.
